Q: Difference between Use Case, Action, and Application Service in DDD A:

In Domain-Driven Design (DDD), an Application Service (e.g. ProductMaintenance) is the technical expression of one or more Use Cases. (Typically it contains / implements multiple use cases, e.g. registerProduct, modifyProduct, and deleteProduct). Whereas an Action (say MassUpdateProductDiscount) is one of the technical executions of the modifyProduct use case

DDD's primary strategic value lies in improving communication and aligning software development with business needs by creating a "Ubiquitous" Language between users and developers.

For your question: Should I create a LoginUseCase, LoginAction, or LoginService? I would say normally it should be something like "AuthenticationManagement" (Application Service), "UserLogin" (Use Case) and "CredentialVerification" (Action). [So the "AuthenticationManagement" Application Service also contains the Use Case of "UserLogout"]

Q: Excel - Skip Blanks and re-display data in Office 365 A:

From Excel 2021 with the FILTER function the required result can be achieved with one of the below formulas.

  1. =FILTER(K102:K111,NOT(ISBLANK(K102:K111))) result in column O

  2. =FILTER(K102:K111,K102:K111<>"") result in column P

The first formula uses the ISBLANK function which works if the cell is really blank.
If the cell contains a formula and the formula result is nothing i.e. an empty string then use the second one, which checks the 0 length string and blank cells and will return the desired result.

Before Excel 2021 this formula can be used:

=INDEX(K102:K111,LARGE(IF(K102:K111<>"",ROW(K102:K111)-101,0),{3;2;1}))

the result of it is in column Q.

Q: Integer.valueOf returns ASCII against a character A:

This is specifically covered by JLS 5.2, Assignment conversion. (Passing a parameter to a method is essentially like assigning a value to a variable.)

Assignment contexts allow the use of one of the following:

...

  • an unboxing conversion (§5.1.8) optionally followed by a widening primitive conversion.

What's happening here is that the Character is being unboxed to char; and then the char is being widened to int.
